newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKER AS PRESSURE PERSISTS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR WEAKER AS PRESSURE PERSISTS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted softer against the U.S. dollar on Friday morning on the back of continued import pressure, dealers said.
"It's really difficult to say where the market is at the moment. The central bank came in a little bit to try and stabilise the dollar but it (intervention) was nothing much," one dealer commented.
"It looks likes there's still fresh import demand coming in."

Dealers said the upsurge in import pressure had stemmed largely from a stament last week by central bank governor Leonard Tsumba who told a local financial newspaper that the local dollar was overvalued by five percent against the U.S. dollar to the detriment of the country's exports.
"According to that statement the Zimbabwe dollar should be at 12.0200 right now," one dealer said on Friday.

At around 0815 GMT the Zimbabwe dollar was a step further towards testing those levels at 11.6000/7000 on the U.S. dollar from 11.5700/6100 at Thursday's close and was also quoted softer on sterling at 19.0200/1200 compared to 18.9425/19.0195.
It was however firmer at 6.2900/3400 from 6.3190/3390 against the mark but slipped to 2.5200/5500 from 2.5110/5180 against South Africa's rand.
